# Copilot instructions for Freeciv

## Build, test, and lint commands

Freeciv supports both Meson and Autotools. Meson is the primary documented
build in `INSTALL`; Autotools details are in `doc/INSTALL.autotools`. Always
use an out-of-tree build directory.

### Meson

```sh
meson setup build -Ddebug=true -Ddefault_library=static
ninja -C build
```

Useful dependency-light variants:

```sh
# Headless/server-oriented build.
meson setup build -Ddebug=true -Dclients=[] -Dfcmp=[] -Dtools=[]

# Development warning check recommended by doc/CodingStyle.
meson setup build -Ddebug=true -Dwerror=true -Doptimization=2
```

Organic-history fork development normally uses the server-only `build-organic`
directory:

```sh
meson setup build-organic '-Dclients=[]' '-Dfcmp=[]' '-Dtools=[]' -Ddebug=true
ninja -C build-organic
```

On macOS or dependency-light hosts, prefer `tools/organic_history/gate.sh`; it
sets the Homebrew/MacPorts `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` fallback and uses the stricter
server-only options `-Daudio=none -Dmwand=false -Dnls=false`.

CI-style Meson coverage, including ruleset checks and an autogame smoke test:

```sh
./scripts/ci-build.sh meson
```

### Autotools

For git checkouts, run `autogen.sh` from the build directory; it creates and
runs `configure`, passing through configure options.

```sh
mkdir build && cd build
../autogen.sh --enable-debug --enable-client=stub --enable-fcmp=cli
make -j"$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null || nproc)"
```

CI-style Autotools coverage:

```sh
./scripts/ci-build.sh autotools
```

### Project checks

Source-style checks are shell scripts under `tests/`; the aggregate Autotools
target writes findings to `tests/check-output`.

```sh
# From a configured Autotools build.
make src-check

# Direct source-tree run.
cd tests && ./src-check.sh
```

Run a single source check directly:

```sh
tests/header_guard.sh "$PWD"
tests/trailing_spaces.sh "$PWD"
tests/check_macros.sh "$PWD"
```

Ruleset tests are generated by Meson custom targets and run from the build
directory:

```sh
cd build
ninja rulesets_not_broken.sh
./rulesets_not_broken.sh              # all developed rulesets
./rulesets_not_broken.sh classic      # single ruleset load test

ninja rulesets_save.sh
./rulesets_save.sh classic            # single ruleset save/stability test

ninja rulesets_upgrade.sh
./rulesets_upgrade.sh
```

Run the server autogame smoke test from a Meson build:

```sh
cd build
./run.sh freeciv-server --Announce none -e -F --read ../scripts/test-autogame.serv
```

Organic-history harnesses live under `tools/organic_history/`. Use the smallest
gate that covers the changed area:

```sh
tools/organic_history/gate.sh                    # build + 20-turn AI ruleset smoke
tools/organic_history/campaign_gate.sh           # gate + 3-seed campaign summary
tools/organic_history/parallel_campaign_gate.sh  # campaign parallelism/isolation
tools/organic_history/mechanics_gate.sh          # disabled-by-default mechanics
tools/organic_history/scenario_gate.sh           # scenario loading/metadata/Lua
tools/organic_history/global_4000_gate.sh        # global 4000 BCE fixture
tools/organic_history/global_4000_lifecycle_gate.sh
```

Run a single organic-history AI smoke directly with:

```sh
python3 tools/organic_history/run_ai_game.py \
  --ruleset-serv data/organic_history.serv \
  --turns 20 \
  --players 4 \
  --output-dir runs/organic_history_local \
  --clean-output-dir
```

## High-level architecture

Freeciv is a client/server game. The server owns most gameplay calculation and
authority; clients are intentionally thin and receive authoritative state over
the packet protocol.

- `server/` contains game authority, command handling, turn progression,
  networking, ruleset loading, savegames, scripting, map generation, and server
  handlers. `server/srv_main.c` drives the turn/input loop.
- `client/` contains GUI-independent client state, packet handling, options,
  map view logic, audio, agents, and Lua client scripting. GUI implementations
  live in `client/gui-*`; cross-GUI entry points are mediated through
  `client/include/*_g.h` and `struct gui_funcs` in `client/gui_interface.h`.
- `common/` holds data structures and game logic shared by client and server:
  map, units, cities, rules concepts, requirements, effects, movement, packets,
  and script core.
- `ai/` is linked into the server. Default AI code is split between `ai/` and
  `server/advisors/`; the latter also supports human-player helpers such as
  autosettlers and autoexplorers.
- `data/` is part of the runtime model, not just assets. Rulesets, nations,
  tilesets, scenarios, sounds, themes, and modpack data are loaded by the
  server/client at runtime; rulesets are the supported way to alter many game
  mechanics without recompilation.
- `tools/` builds support executables such as `freeciv-ruleup`,
  `freeciv-manual`, `freeciv-ruledit`, and modpack installers.
- `utility/` provides portability and infrastructure wrappers used across the
  tree; prefer these over raw libc/platform calls where equivalents exist.
- The organic-history fork layers its ruleset, Lua diagnostics/mechanics, and
  authored scenario data under `data/organic_history/`. Harnesses, parsers,
  experiment runners, gates, and profiles live under `tools/organic_history/`;
  design/task notes live under `docs/organic_history/`; generated run outputs go
  under `runs/`.

Network packets are defined in `common/networking/packets.def` and generated by
`common/generate_packets.py` into common/client/server `*_gen.[ch]` files.
When adding or changing packets, update `packets.def`; only edit the generator
if the generated protocol machinery itself changes.

Several enums and bitvectors are generated from `gen_headers/enums/*.def` by
`gen_headers/generate_enums.py`. Update the `.def` source rather than generated
headers.

The canonical organic-history global data layer is
`data/organic_history/history/earth_global_4000.json`. Regenerate/check derived
history artifacts with:

```sh
python3 tools/organic_history/generate_history_artifacts.py --check
```

## Key conventions

- C code is mostly C89 with selected C99 features; Qt code is C++ but follows
  the same house style where practical. Headers must remain C++ compatible.
- Include order in `.c`/`.cpp` files is structured: optional `fc_config.h`
  first, then system headers, then commented groups such as `/* utility */`,
  `/* common */`, `/* client/include */`, `/* client */`, `/* server */`, and
  finally the matching local header.
- New C code uses K&R style, 2-space indentation, no tabs, braces for
  conditionals/loops, and lines up to 77 characters. Avoid reformatting
  untouched code.
- Functions implemented in `.c` files should have the repository's Doxygen
  banner comment above the implementation. Translator comments must start with
  `TRANS:` immediately before or on the same line as `_()`, `N_()`, `Q_()`, or
  `PL_()`.
- Use Freeciv wrappers and macros: `fc_malloc`, `fc_realloc`, `fc_calloc`,
  `fc_strdup`, `FC_FREE`, `fc_fopen`, `fc_strlcpy`, `fc_strcasecmp`,
  `fc_snprintf`, `log_*`, and `fc_assert*` from `utility/`. Do not use raw
  `assert()` or `die()`.
- In C code, boolean values are `TRUE` and `FALSE`; in C++ use `true` and
  `false`. Include `utility/support.h` when a C file needs `bool`.
- Use `fc__fallthrough` for intentional switch fallthrough. Avoid `default`
  cases where an exhaustive enum switch should let the compiler warn.
- Freeciv collections commonly use generated `*_list_iterate(...) { ... }
  *_list_iterate_end;` macros from `utility/speclist.h`. Use the corresponding
  safe iterator variant when the current loop may delete list entries.
- Map code must use topology-aware helpers and iterators such as
  `map_pos_to_tile()`, `adjc_iterate`, `cardinal_adjc_iterate`,
  `whole_map_iterate`, and distance helpers; do not hand-roll adjacent tile
  loops from `x/y` offsets.
- Ruleset files must be UTF-8, and translatable ruleset text should be
  American English ASCII. Existing rulesets in `data/` are canonical examples;
  keep ruleset-dependent behavior synchronized with server loading and tests.
- For organic-history work, do not edit upstream rulesets such as
  `data/classic`, `data/civ2civ3`, or `data/sandbox` directly; modify the
  `data/organic_history` copy.
- Client/server communication uses generated `send_packet_*`,
  `receive_packet_*`, and `handle_*` paths. Reuse existing generic packet
  types where appropriate, and respect packet capability/add-cap/remove-cap
  rules for compatibility.
- Organic-history mechanics must remain off by default. Enable them only in
  explicit campaign/server commands such as
  `lua cmd organic_history_mechanics_enabled = true`; bootstrap packages are
  separately gated by `organic_history_bootstrap_enabled`.
- Add or preserve diagnostics/metrics before tuning organic-history mechanics.
  Treat historical data as "historical gravity, not destiny": consume
  `historicalGravity` gates, escape routes, and lifecycle archetype data instead
  of scripting outcomes purely from actor/date matches.
- Scenario fixtures live under `data/organic_history/scenarios/` and are loaded
  through `run_ai_game.py --load-scenario`, which passes
  `--ruleset organic_history` so ruleset Lua diagnostics stay active. Regenerate
  authored fixtures with
  `python3 tools/organic_history/create_scenario_fixture.py --include-v1 --all-v1-plans`.
